defects.source_says: EO 12608 (52 FR 34617) is dated September 9, 1987 (the held text's signing date 1987-09-09; the OFR note reads 'Amended by: EO 12608, September 9, 1987'). The clause's own judgment_reason says the signing date is used because EO 12608 states no separate effective date, so the event date should be 1987-09-09; 1984-09-09 is wrong and internally inconsistent.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12608.txt sec. 31 (amends EO 12322 sec. 2(b)); no effective-date clause found
42 U.S.C. 1962 note (release point 119-121): as amended by EO 12608, text printed in full
OFR notes: EO 12322 Revokes EO 12113; Amended by EO 12608; EO 12141 Revoked by EO 12322
reasons: Identity (EO 12322, September 17, 1981, 46 FR 46561), quotes and the eight-clause inventory check out, and the operative predicate for sections 1-3 is supported by the current 42 U.S.C. 1962 note and the 43 CFR 404.51 hit; no held Revoked/Superseded note exists for EO 12322. EO 12608 sec. 31 is correctly identified as an amendment of sec. 2(b). But the later event recording that amendment carries effective_date 1984-09-09, three years before EO 12608 was signed and contrary to the clause's reason that the signing date (1987-09-09) is used. A wrong later-event date is a dated-fact error; rejected. Note: the OFR note that EO 12322 also revoked EO 12141 (an amendment of EO 12113) is consistent with sec. 4's 'as amended' and is not a defect.
